current_example.problem: Find, in radians, the argument of $z=-1+\textrm{i}\sqrt{3}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226152/assets/1bd35c5350e1dc1988cf98b8598a350701ef0b2a02a053b97ae2c89726de50c6.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\dfrac{\pi}{2}<        \arg(z)<        \pi.$ If $\alpha$ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1} \\ \alpha  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta=\arg(z) = \pi - \dfrac\pi 3 = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}.
$$
